# Consolidate proxy log-file discovery into one shared helper

**Headline:** Four analysis/operations scripts still carry a dot-only, gzip-blind proxy-log
discovery copy (a fifth duplicates already-patched logic), so dash-named logrotate files and
`.gz` files are silently dropped. Extract one lightweight project-owned helper and migrate all
five call sites to it, with regression tests for both naming schemes and both plain/compressed
variants.

## Problem Statement

`LP-0MTYARXXZ002VNF5` fixed proxy-log discovery inside the `proxy-usage-analysis` skill:
the deployment writes the same log stream under **two** rotation schemes — in-process
`TimedRotatingFileHandler` (`proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HH`) and a logrotate safety net
(`proxy.log-YYYY-MM-DD_HH`) — and both may be gzip-compressed. Four sibling scripts each define
their own discovery and still match only the dot scheme, so they silently omit dash-named
files (which carry the whole daytime window) and ignore compressed rotated files. A fifth
script (`slot_persistence_harness.py`) was patched in isolation for dash + `.gz` but keeps a
duplicate local implementation. Because the logic is copied, every naming/compression change
re-breaks the scripts that were not touched.

## Users & User Stories

- **Proxy operations engineer:** "When I correlate slot-persistence failures, compact sessions,
  or analyse context distribution over a day, I need every rotated log file — dot-named,
  dash-named, plain or `.gz` — to be read, so my totals are not silently short."
- **On-call investigator:** "When I run a correlation script during an incident, I want it to
  use the same discovery as the usage-analysis skill, so I do not have to remember which script
  is currently broken."
- **Maintainer:** "When rotation naming or compression changes again, I want to update exactly
  one helper, not five copies."

## Existing State

| Location | Current discovery | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py:229-238` | local `discover_log_files`, `name == "proxy.log" or startswith("proxy.log.")` | misses dash; no shared source |
| `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py:233-239` | same local copy | misses dash |
| `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py:67-69` | imports `discover_log_files` from `analyze_context_distribution` | inherits the gap |
| `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py:81-84` | `log_dir.glob("proxy.log.*")`, plain open only | misses dash **and** `.gz` |
| `scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py:60-76` | local dot+dash glob with `.gz` opener | correct, but duplicate logic |

The skill already has a correct reference implementation:
`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — `open_log_text` (lines 568-579) and a
scheme-aware `discover_log_files` (lines 609+). `proxy/scripts/extract_aug3_errors.py:53-61`
shows a precedent for importing it via `sys.path`.

Note: the seed's `proxy/utils.py` is in fact `proxy/proxy/utils.py`; its `prune_logs`
(line 622) uses `glob("proxy.log.*")` but is the production retention/compression path and is
**out of scope** (logrotate owns dash-file pruning — see Decision D3).

## Desired Change

Create one lightweight, project-owned module — `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py`
(plus `scripts/lib/__init__.py`) — importable from both `proxy/scripts/*` and repo-root
`scripts/*` without pulling in the heavy `proxy.proxy.utils` dependencies (`httpx`, `yaml`,
`proxy.session`). It exposes:

- `discover_proxy_log_files(log_dir: Path) -> list[Path]` — live `proxy.log` plus rotated
  `proxy.log.*` (dot) and `proxy.log-*` (dash), plain or `.gz`, sorted by name; `[]` when
  `log_dir` is not a directory.
- `open_proxy_log_text(path: Path)` — open a proxy log for text reading, transparently
  gzip-decompressing `.gz` (mirrors the skill's `open_log_text` semantics).
- `iter_proxy_log_lines(log_dir: Path)` — convenience generator yielding `(path, line)`
  across all discovered files, for the two root scripts that consume lines.

Migrate all five call sites to this helper (delete the four local/duplicated discovery copies
and the root script's plain-only opener). Update the existing per-script tests and add
dash/`.gz` regression coverage.

This consolidates the **project** scripts onto one helper. The skill remains the reference for
its own package; the new module is self-contained so project tooling has no runtime dependency
on `.pi/` agent infrastructure.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Single shared helper.** `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` defines discovery (live + dot + dash,
   plain + `.gz`) and gzip-aware opening once; its unit tests cover each naming/compression
   variant and the "not a directory" case.
2. **All five call sites migrated.** `analyze_context_distribution.py`,
   `run_compaction_experiment.py`, `correlate_oversized_sessions.py`,
   `slot-persistence-correlate.py`, and `slot_persistence_harness.py` use the shared helper;
   no local dot-only discovery copy remains (`grep -n 'startswith("proxy.log.")'` and
   `grep -n 'glob("proxy.log.*")'` in those scripts return nothing). `proxy/proxy/utils.py`
   and the `.pi/` skill are explicitly out of scope.
3. **Regression tests prove dash + `.gz` data is read, per script.** At least one new test per
   script feeds a dash-named and/or `.gz` rotated file and asserts its content contributes to
   the script's output (not merely that discovery lists it); all existing tests for these
   scripts still pass. New shared-helper tests live at `tests/test_proxy_logs.py`.
4. **Documentation updated.** New module and changed functions have clear docstrings explaining
   the two rotation schemes and gzip handling, the changed scripts' module docstrings reflect
   the shared helper, and this work item's description records the design decision. All related
   documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any
   relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run via `/skill:test` (cached
   full-suite runner); the proxy suite (`proxy/tests/`) and root suite (`tests/`) must both be
   green.

### Verification commands

```bash
# New helper unit tests + root script regression
test -f scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py && python3 -m pytest tests/test_proxy_logs.py tests/test_slot_persistence_correlate.py -q
# Proxy script regressions (run from proxy/)
(cd proxy && python3 -m pytest tests/test_analyze_context_distribution.py tests/test_compaction_experiment.py tests/test_correlate_oversized_sessions.py tests/test_slot_persistence_harness.py -q)
# AC2: no local dot-only discovery copy in the five in-scope scripts
grep -n 'startswith("proxy.log.")' proxy/scripts/*.py scripts/slot*.py || echo 'clean'
grep -n 'glob("proxy.log.\*")' scripts/slot*.py || echo 'clean'
# Full suite (cached)
/skill:test
```

## Constraints

- Do **not** edit `.pi/` (agent infrastructure). The shared module is project-owned; the skill
  stays as-is.
- Keep the helper dependency-light: standard library only (`gzip`, `pathlib`).
- Preserve each script's observable output format and CLI; this is a discovery/opening refactor,
  not a behaviour change beyond including the previously dropped files.
- Preserve the existing per-line timestamp filtering as the authoritative window boundary; the
  helper must not filter by filename-encoded time (files routinely hold data past their encoded
  rotation time).
- Keep sorted-by-name ordering consistent with the current scripts.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` — **new** shared discovery + gzip-aware opening helper.
- `scripts/lib/__init__.py` — **new** package marker so `from lib.proxy_logs import ...` works
  from both `scripts/*` and `proxy/scripts/*`.
- `tests/test_proxy_logs.py` — **new** unit tests for the helper (live/dot/dash × plain/`.gz`).
- `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` — drop local `discover_log_files`; import helper (alias to `discover_log_files`); route `iter_log_lines` opener through `open_proxy_log_text`.
- `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` — same migration.
- `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py` — import discovery from the shared helper directly instead of via `analyze_context_distribution`.
- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py` — replace `_iter_proxy_logs` dot-only/plain-only implementation with the shared helper.
- `scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py` — replace `_iter_proxy_files`/proxy branch with the shared helper; leave llama-log functions untouched.
- `proxy/tests/test_analyze_context_distribution.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_experiment.py`, `proxy/tests/test_correlate_oversized_sessions.py`, `tests/test_slot_persistence_correlate.py` — add dash/`.gz` regression cases; `proxy/tests/test_slot_persistence_harness.py` already covers dash + `.gz`.

### Import mechanics (both trees)

- Root scripts run with `scripts/` as `sys.path[0]`, so `from lib.proxy_logs import ...`
  resolves the local package.
- `proxy/scripts/*` insert the repo-root `scripts/` directory on `sys.path` before importing
  (mirroring the existing `extract_aug3_errors.py` pattern) and then `from lib.proxy_logs import ...`.
- `proxy/tests/*` already add `proxy/scripts` to `sys.path`; the shared import resolves through
  the script's own path insertion.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption (D1):** All five call sites are in scope (per producer answer 1a); the four
  broken scripts are the minimum, the harness migration removes the last duplicate.
- **Assumption (D2):** The helper lives in a project-owned `scripts/lib/` module (producer
  answer 2c); the skill's logic is the behavioural reference but is not imported at runtime.
- **Assumption (D3):** `proxy/proxy/utils.py::prune_logs` is a non-goal. It only prunes/compresses
  the in-process dot scheme by design; logrotate owns dash-file pruning/compression. Revisit in a
  follow-up only if retention of dash files is later delegated away from logrotate.
- **Risk — import path fragility:** a `lib` package name is generic; sys.path order matters.
  Mitigation: `scripts/lib/__init__.py`, explicit path insertion in proxy scripts, and tests that
  invoke both a root script (subprocess) and the proxy scripts as modules.
- **Risk — hidden behaviour change:** including dash files changes report totals (expected and
  desired). Mitigation: per-script regression tests assert the delta from a dash/`.gz` fixture.
- **Risk — scope creep:** opportunity to also make `prune_logs` dash-aware, or to import the
  skill directly, is recorded here as a linked follow-up rather than folded into this task.
- **Assumption:** existing per-line timestamp filtering remains correct and authoritative; the
  helper performs no time-based filtering.

## Related work

- `LP-0MTYARXXZ002VNF5` — proxy-usage-analysis: discover_log_files drops logrotate dash-named
  daily files (completed). The originating fix; this item extends it to the project scripts.
- `LP-0MSISZS1O004KJRR` — proxy-usage-analysis file discovery silently excludes rotated logs
  whose name-encoded time precedes window start (completed). Establishes "include all rotated
  files; per-line filtering is authoritative".
- `LP-0MSNKMXIK004P7TL` — Create log rotation / prune retention for llama-proxy logs
  (completed). Establishes the two rotation mechanisms and logrotate's pruning role (basis for D3).
- `proxy/scripts/extract_aug3_errors.py` — precedent for importing the skill's `log_parser` via
  `sys.path` (referenced, not adopted).

## Decision record (producer input, 2026-09-26)

- **D1 — Scope:** all five call sites, including the already-patched
  `scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py`, share the helper (answer: 1a).
- **D2 — Location:** create a project-owned lightweight shared module rather than importing the
  skill or extending `.pi/` (answer: 2c); chosen path `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py`.
- **D3 — `prune_logs`:** excluded from the dot-only grep check; logrotate owns dash-file
  retention (answer: "your call").

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1:** "Scope: four listed scripts, or all five call sites including
  `scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py`?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26): "1. a"** — all five
  call sites. Source: interactive reply on the producer-review comment
  `LP-C0MUHY4SGT003BT24`. This resolves the AC2 (four) vs Proposed-remediation (five) contradiction.
- **Q2:** "Where should the shared helper live — import the skill's `log_parser` read-only,
  extend the skill's `log_parser.py`, or create a project-owned module?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26): "2. c"** — project-owned shared module. Source: same reply.
  Research: `proxy/proxy/utils.py` has heavy deps (`httpx`, `yaml`, `proxy.session`), so a
  stdlib-only `scripts/lib` module was selected; `extract_aug3_errors.py` is the skill-import
  precedent that was considered and not adopted.
- **Q3:** "Is `proxy/proxy/utils.py::prune_logs` in scope for the 'no dot-only copy' check, or
  excluded because logrotate handles dash pruning?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26): "3. your
  call"** — decision D3: excluded; recorded as a potential follow-up. Source: same reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MSXZ06M5007CPN6** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/scripts/llama-proxy-logrotate:10 — Expected a statement (invalid-syntax) (completed)
- **LP-0MSXZ072M0085AF5** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/scripts/llama-proxy-logrotate:12 — Expected `,`, found name (invalid-syntax) (completed)
- **LP-0MSXZ07AP000EBO7** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/scripts/llama-proxy-logrotate:12 — Expected `,`, found int (invalid-syntax) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac2, acceptance, add, again, agent (+340 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac2, acceptance, add, again, agent (+340 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: ac2, acceptance, add, again, agent (+340 more)

---

## Plan: changelog (2026-09-26)

- **Planning completed** — `plan` skill decomposed this item into four
  dependency-ordered children and advanced the stage to `plan_complete`.
- **Intent preserved:** the intake brief already carried the design decisions
  (D1–D3); planning materialised them without changing scope.
- **Children created:**
  - `LP-0MUIEK483002TZ54` — Add shared proxy log discovery + gzip-open helper (no deps).
  - `LP-0MUIEK47X000WL2C` — Migrate proxy/scripts consumers to shared log helper
    (depends on `LP-0MUIEK483002TZ54`).
  - `LP-0MUIEK66C003VGO1` — Migrate root scripts consumers to shared log helper
    (depends on `LP-0MUIEK483002TZ54`).

- **Review outcome:** all four children pass `**Key Files:**` validation; the
  AC coverage review returns `proceed` (note: the parent ACs are a numbered

### Plan appendix (2026-09-26)

- **Q:** Does planning need new producer input? **Answer (plan skill):** none.
  The intake appendix already resolved the only open forks: scope (D1 — all

  `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py`), and `prune_logs` exclusion (D3). No new

# Intake Brief: When a request cannot be processed because there are no available models include a retry timer (LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI)

## Headline

Verify, end-to-end, that when the proxy cannot process a request because every
model is unavailable it returns the "All providers exhausted" 503 carrying a
truthful retry timer (a `Retry-After` header and a matching `retry_after` body
field derived from real availability), and that the client can actually act on
it. The proxy emission is already implemented by the overnight-exhaustion epic;
this item proves the composed contract and tracks the one remaining client-side
gap (the 60 s clamp) in a linked ContextHub work item.

## Problem statement

Clients reach an upstream LLM through this proxy. When every provider that can
serve a request is unavailable — in cooldown, outside its `available_times`
window, or usage-limit quarantined — the proxy rejects the request with a 503
whose `error` prose is `"All providers exhausted"`. For an unattended agent
(herdr worker / Pi session) to recover automatically, that rejection must tell
it *how long* to wait, and the client must actually wait that long.

The proxy side was delivered by the overnight-exhaustion epic
(LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO): the generic and time-window exhaustion 503s emit a
`Retry-After` header plus a matching `retry_after` body field computed by
`_compute_retry_after` from real availability (cooldowns, window edges,
usage-limit resets). What is not owned anywhere is a single **end-to-end
verification** that the composed "no models available" retry contract holds and
fails if any part regresses. Separately, the client clamps an applied
`Retry-After` to 60 s (`retry-logic.ts` `maxDelayMs = 60000`), so a truthful
multi-hour overnight `retry_after` is never actually waited out — this needs a
linked ContextHub change.

## Users

- **Local agent (herdr worker / Pi session)** — the primary beneficiary. Must
  receive a truthful retry timer and be able to wait until models return instead
  of surfacing `Unrecognized error:` or retrying every 60 s through an
  overnight gap.
- **Proxy operator / on-call engineer** — needs confidence that any regression
  in the exhaustion retry contract is caught by an automated end-to-end test.
- **ContextHub maintainers** — need the client-side gap recorded and linked
  (WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM) so the proxy's honest timer is honoured.

### Example user stories

- As a local agent, I want the "All providers exhausted" 503 to carry a truthful
  `Retry-After`/`retry_after` so I know when to come back.
- As an operator, I want an end-to-end test that fails if the retry timer is
  dropped or becomes untruthful (e.g. hardcoded 60 s, or 0 while providers are
  blocked).
- As a ContextHub maintainer, I want the 60 s clamp tracked so the client waits
  out a multi-hour retry hint.

## Scope (producer-confirmed)

Per the producer's answers to the intake questions (Appendix):

- **Q1 = (b):** this item is an **end-to-end verification** of the whole
  "no models available" retry contract **on the proxy** (not a new feature that
  adds retry hints to further paths).
- **Q2 = (b):** the contract in scope is **only the "All providers exhausted"
  503** (generic `code: all_exhausted` and its time-window variant
  `code: outside_time_window`). The local slot-exhaustion 429 and the router
  concurrency-limit 503 are **out of scope**.
- **Q3 = (a):** the proxy must emit the **true** wait, and the client must be
  able to honour a long wait — the client-side 60 s clamp is tracked in the
  linked ContextHub item **WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM**.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Retry timer present and consistent:** A deterministic end-to-end test
  drives the in-process proxy with every provider unavailable and asserts the
  terminal `503` "All providers exhausted" response carries **both** a
  `Retry-After` HTTP header (integer delta-seconds) and a `retry_after` JSON body
  field, with the **same value**.
- **AC2 — Timeless truthfulness:** The asserted `retry_after` equals the real
  soonest availability (the maximum of cooldown durations, `available_times`
  window edges, and usage-limit reset times), is positive whenever a provider is
  genuinely blocked, and is `0` only when availability exists. The test pins the
  clock/value so the assertion is deterministic.
- **AC3 — Both exhaustion variants covered:** The verification covers the generic
  `code: "all_exhausted"` path and the time-window `code: "outside_time_window"`
  path (both are "All providers exhausted" 503s), asserting the same retry-timer
  contract on each.
- **AC4 — Client-recognition contract intact:** The response retains
  `error == "All providers exhausted"` and a stable `code`, and the existing
  exhaustion-contract tests still pass (additive-only; no prose/code change).
- **AC5 — No hold longer than the timer:** When a chain-hold would exceed the
  retry timer, the exhaustion response is surfaced immediately with the timer
  rather than held beyond it (bounded by `retry_after`). Verified in the same or
  a paired test.
- **AC6 — Client gap linked:** The ContextHub item WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM exists and
  is referenced from this item, so the proxy's honest multi-hour timer can be
  honoured by the client rather than clamped to 60 s.
- **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, `proxy/README.md` (the exhaustion/retry
  contract section), and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC8 — Full suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Additive-only contract:** do not remove or reword the existing `error` prose
  or `code` values — older clients key on them (epic constraint
  LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO).
- **Verification, not availability policy:** do not widen `available_times` or
  wake a provider outside its window to make a test pass.
- **No proxy restart:** verification runs in-process; never kill the proxy.
- **Out of scope:** local slot-exhaustion 429, router concurrency-limit 503,
  compaction-gate 429, session single-flight 429 (per Q2); client code changes
  (ContextHub, per Q3).

## Existing state

- `_build_exhausted_response` and `_build_time_window_exhausted_response`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`) emit `Retry-After` + `retry_after` on the 503,
  plus retained `error`/`code`/`diagnostics`/`unavailable_providers`.
- `_compute_retry_after` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`) computes the honest value
  from cooldowns (`_provider_unavailable_until`), `available_times` window edges
  (`_seconds_until_next_window`), and usage-limit resets (`_usage_reset_at`).
- `_bounded_chain_hold_seconds` / `_exhaustion_retry_after`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`) bound the chain-hold by the response's real
  `Retry-After` and surface the response immediately when the timer exceeds the
  hold budget (LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08).
- The epic's integration verification item LP-0MUI68NTH004SZMG (blocked) already
  composes overnight remotes-out-of-window + usage-limit quarantine + local-lease
  denial and asserts an accurate 503; the retry timer is one of its assertions.
  This item's focused retry-timer verification should reference or extend that
  test rather than duplicate it (see Risks).
- Client side (ContextHub `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/`):
  `retry-logic.ts` parses `Retry-After`/`Retry-After-Ms` headers and the body
  `retry_after`, but clamps the applied delay to `maxDelayMs = 60000`; the retry
  loop (`register-recovery.ts`) is otherwise unbounded.

## Desired change

1. Add one deterministic end-to-end proxy test (or extend LP-0MUI68NTH004SZMG's
   test) proving the composed "All providers exhausted" retry contract:
   truthful `Retry-After` + `retry_after`, both exhaustion variants, no
   over-long hold, client-recognition prose/code intact.
2. Reference the linked ContextHub item WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM from this item (and
   vice versa) so the client-side 60 s clamp is tracked.
3. Update `proxy/README.md` (and code comments) to state the verified contract
   and the client expectation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_exhausted_response` (~line 2955),
  `_build_time_window_exhausted_response` (~line 3015), `_compute_retry_after`
  (~line 2257), `_bounded_chain_hold_seconds` / `_exhaustion_retry_after`
  (~line 4910).
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`, `proxy/tests/test_exhaustion_error_code.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_retry_after_bound.py` — extend/add the E2E
  retry-timer assertions.
- `proxy/README.md` — exhaustion / retry contract section (~line 690).
- Cross-repo: ContextHub `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts`
  (the linked item WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM, not edited here).

## Related work

| Item | Relationship |
|------|-------------|
| LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO — Epic: Overnight remote-chain exhaustion | Parent context; delivered the proxy-side retry contract this item verifies. |
| LP-0MUI68NTH004SZMG — E2E verification: overnight-gap exhaustion contract | Related/blocks: composes the overnight-gap 503; this item's retry-timer verification should reference/extend it, not duplicate it. |
| LP-0MT654ISW002QVH4 — Honest Retry-After: emit real provider availability windows | Predecessor: truthful `retry_after`/`Retry-After` on the exhaustion 503. |
| LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G — Exhaustion 503: stable machine-readable error code | Predecessor: `code` discriminators. |
| LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08 — Chain-hold: bound hold duration by the real `retry_after` | Predecessor: no over-long hold. |
| **WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM** — Honour long server `Retry-After` hints (do not clamp to 60 s) | Linked client-side item (ContextHub) created from Q3(a); tracks the remaining gap. |

# Auto-derive large-context routing thresholds (physical clamp + latency-derived economic ceiling)

## Goal (user story)

As a proxy operator, I want the large-context **warm** routing threshold to auto-derive from the active model's context size and slot count — using a physical per-slot clamp plus a latency-derived economic ceiling — so that changing the slot count or the model context size never requires manual threshold recalculation, while never routing latency-destroying warm contexts local. The **cold** (new-token) threshold stays a fixed per-mode economic value.

## Problem statement

`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` is a single absolute value (100,000) shared by every mode profile and clamped at runtime to the physical per-slot capacity:

```
effective_warm = min(configured_warm, per_slot_cap)
per_slot_cap   = local_model_ctx_size // slots - 4096
```

The same configured value therefore has wildly different effective meaning per profile, and operators must manually recalculate it whenever the slot schedule or model context size changes:

| Profile | Slots | Per-slot cap | Configured warm | Effective warm | % of cap |
|---------|-------|--------------|-----------------|----------------|----------|
| fast    | 1     | 258,048      | 100,000         | 100,000        | 38.7%    |
| (2-slot)| 2     | 126,976      | 100,000         | 100,000        | 78.7%    |
| cheap   | 3     | 83,285       | 100,000         | 83,285         | 100%     |

The 2026-09-16 design review measured that this is **not** simply a capacity problem: prompt-eval throughput falls from ~676 tok/s at 2K context to ~37 tok/s at 100K, and a full 100K cold prefill extrapolates to 20-45 minutes of single-slot occupancy. A uniform ratio that scales the warm cap with per-slot capacity would imply ~20 tok/s prefill and hour-scale slot monopolisation on the 1-slot fast profile. The warm cap is an **economic/latency** limit driven by absolute context length, while the per-slot clamp is a **physical** capacity limit. The two must be modelled separately.

## Users

- **As a proxy operator**, I want thresholds derived from `local_model_ctx_size` and slot count so a profile change (e.g. a smaller model or a 2-slot schedule) needs no manual threshold arithmetic.
- **As a capacity planner**, I want a documented, configurable economic ceiling so the latency/utilisation trade-off is explicit and auditable.
- **As an on-call engineer**, I want startup logs to show the computed clamp, ceiling and effective thresholds per mode so a misconfiguration is visible immediately.

## Existing state

- `effective_per_slot_threshold(ctx_size, slots)` returns `ctx_size // slots - 4096` (0 when not meaningful) — `proxy/proxy/provider.py`.
- `_effective_large_context_thresholds(config)` clamps **only** warm to the per-slot cap; cold is deliberately left unclamped so the `(cold, warm]` band is non-empty for the `cached_ratio` check (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).
- The hard-routing caps (fast 70K / cheap 61.4K) were reverted to dynamic by LP-0MTLB1LK80098R43; the per-slot clamp + warm config are the only binding values.
- Current effective values: fast warm 100,000 (38.7% of cap), cheap warm 83,285 (100% of cap), cold 38,000 / 42,000.
- Cache warmth is bimodal (42.5% cold at 0.0-0.1, 46.1% fully warm at 0.95-1.0), so the warm cap binds almost exclusively on fully-warm requests; eviction can invalidate a warm claim.

## Desired change

Adopt a **3-term model** for the warm threshold:

1. **Physical term** — the per-slot clamp `local_model_ctx_size // slots - 4096` (unchanged, already correct).
2. **Economic term** — a latency-derived ceiling that scales with the **model** context size (not slot count): `economic_ceiling = round(local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio × local_model_ctx_size)`. The shipped ratio is `0.3815` (= 100000 / 262144), calibrated to the ~37 tok/s @100K throughput floor.
3. **Effective warm** = `min(physical_term, economic_ceiling)`.

The per-slot term dominates when `slots >= 3` (the clamp binds); the economic term dominates when `slots == 1`.

The absolute `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`, when set, is retained as an additional upper bound (`economic_ceiling = min(ratio × ctx, warm_threshold)`) for backward compatibility; a ratio of 0 falls back to the absolute value, and both 0 disables the warm cap as today.

The **cold** threshold remains a fixed per-mode economic new-token value (fast 38,000 / cheap 42,000), is not clamped or scaled, and the `(cold, warm]` band stays non-empty.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new economic-ceiling helper computes `round(local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio × local_model_ctx_size)`, capped by `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` when that is > 0; returns 0 (disabled) when both inputs are 0.
- [ ] `_effective_large_context_thresholds()` resolves warm as `min(effective_per_slot_threshold(ctx_size, slots), economic_ceiling)`; with the shipped config (ratio 0.3815, ctx 262144) the computed values are fast (1 slot) = 100,000, 2-slot = 100,000, cheap (3 slots) = 83,285.
- [ ] The economic ceiling scales with model context size: with `local_model_ctx_size = 131072` and 1 slot the effective warm is ~50,000 (linear scaling test).
- [ ] The cold threshold remains a fixed per-mode value, is never clamped or scaled by per-slot capacity, and the `(cold, warm]` band is non-empty for every shipped profile (regression guard for LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).
- [ ] Startup validation logs, for the active mode, the computed physical clamp, economic ceiling and effective warm/cold thresholds; the existing `min_local_routing_threshold` warning still fires when the physical clamp falls below the minimum.
- [ ] Unit tests assert: 1/2/3-slot scaling; ceiling scaling with model ctx; ratio=0 falls back to the absolute override; both 0 disables; band non-collapse; and that fast warm never exceeds the economic ceiling even when the per-slot clamp is larger.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (config comments in `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/config-fast.yaml`, `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`; `docs/llama-router.md`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The warm threshold must **not** be raised above the latency-derived economic ceiling — measured prefill throughput makes hour-scale single-slot monopolisation unacceptable (design review, 2026-09-16).
- The cold threshold must not be scaled with per-slot capacity (preserves the `(cold, warm]` band).
- Config stays mode-overlay compatible and must not require manual per-profile recalculation when slot count or model ctx changes.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the ship skill).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `effective_per_slot_threshold`, `_effective_large_context_thresholds`, `_get_warm_cache_threshold`; add the economic-ceiling helper and ratio reader.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — add `local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio` (0.3815) and update the warm/cold threshold comments.
- `proxy/config-fast.yaml`, `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — document the derived values; no manual absolute recalculation.
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py`, `proxy/proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy/session.py` — consumers of `effective_per_slot_threshold` (verify no behaviour regression).
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py` / startup validation path — log the computed clamp, ceiling and effective thresholds.
- `proxy/tests/` — new/updated tests for proportional scaling, ceiling scaling, band non-collapse and startup logging.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the economic-ceiling ratio `0.3815` (100000 / 262144) is the correct runtime calibration encoding the ~37 tok/s @100K throughput floor. Implementation may also expose `local_large_context_min_prefill_tps` for documentation/validation, but the ratio is the runtime source.
- **Risk (cache-warmth reliability):** warmth is bimodal and eviction can invalidate a "warm" claim; mitigation: keep the ceiling conservative and rely on the session persistence cap (`session_slot_max_prompt_tokens`).
- **Risk (band collapse):** clamping cold with warm would make the `cached_ratio` check unreachable; AC4 guards this.
- **Risk (model ctx mismatch):** `local_model_ctx_size` must match the local model's `ctx-size` in `models.ini`; startup validation should surface a mismatch.
- **Risk (scope creep):** per-request dynamic ceilings or tokenizer-accuracy changes (LP-0MSEGPO77005CYCQ) are out of scope — record as linked work instead.

## Related work

- LP-0MU1RXF6R004S8XL (completed) — documented that the threshold does not scale with per-slot capacity; decision deferred to this item.
- LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 (completed) — introduced the per-slot clamp (physical term).
- LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S (completed, reverted) — hard-routing cap implementation; removed by LP-0MTLB1LK80098R43.
- LP-0MTLB1LK80098R43 (completed) — reverted the hard caps to dynamic derivation.
- LP-0MU5A4QBR003YJM0 (completed) — cheap mode serves economically-bypassed large contexts locally.
- LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP (completed) — collapsed-band bug the design must not reintroduce.
- Parent epic LP-0MU1S617L002Q9PR — root cause #3 (large-context routing threshold does not scale with per-slot capacity).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MQS6MPCY000A1DN** – Phase 1: Core JobScheduler - slot state tracking (completed)
- **LP-0MTQYIK4Z008XF2V** – Change the number of queued local items between fast and cheap (completed)
- **LP-0MT1F4JAK0057OJN** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MSY0V4ZO002ANPL-set-cheap-mode-cold-threshold-to-38000-w/proxy/config-cheap.yaml:122 — Unexpected indentation (invalid-syntax) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absolute, acceptance, actual, adding, applied (+110 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absolute, acceptance, actual, adding, applied (+110 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absolute, acceptance, actual, adding, applied (+110 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Design model — adopt the 3-term model (physical per-slot clamp + latency-derived economic ceiling), keep the uniform-ratio design, or a hybrid?" — Answer (operator@producer): Recommended option **A** — adopt the 3-term model. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-30 (`as recommended`).
- Q2: "How should the economic ceiling be derived?" — Answer (operator@producer): Recommended option **A** — derive from the prefill-throughput floor and scale linearly with `local_model_ctx_size` (262,144 ctx => ~100K; 131,072 ctx => ~50K). Source: interactive reply 2026-09-30.
- Q3: "Should the cold (new-token) threshold scale with per-slot capacity?" — Answer (operator@producer): Recommended option **A** — no; keep the fixed per-mode economic value (fast 38,000 / cheap 42,000) so the `(cold, warm]` band stays non-empty. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-30.
- Q4 (additional finding): "Priority — creator set `critical`; the acceptance guide lands this at `high` (major behaviour change blocking the parent epic, but not security, data loss or a broken build)." — Answer (operator@producer): accepted the recommendation — priority set to `high`. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-30.
- Citation for the design-review evidence (Q1/Q2 rationale): work-item comment by `agent` dated 2026-09-16T15:27:22Z on LP-0MU466L1X003RTHN.

## Goal

Make the bounded contention queue cover requests denied by the **prefill-aware guard**, not just requests denied by the generating-only pool, so prefill-saturated requests wait for a slot instead of falling back to remote.

## Problem (code-inspection finding)

Two different occupancy gates decide whether a local dispatch happens:

1. **provider.py in-front-of-router check** (`_local_concurrency_info` → `_get_local_concurrency_info`): returns the **generating-only** count.
   ```python
   cur_local, max_local = _local_concurrency_info(config, endpoint=local_endpoint)
   if cur_local >= max_local:
       _maybe_queue_for_local_slot(...)   # queue engages
   ```
2. **router.py dispatch-lease check** (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch`): denies on EITHER
   ```python
   if _generating_count >= max_local: return (False, ...)
   if _prefill_count >= max_local:    return (False, ...)   # <-- prefill gate
   ```

The contention queue's wake predicate only watches the **generating** count:
```python
slot_free_check=lambda: _get_local_concurrency_info(config)[0] < max_local
```

So a request that arrives while a **prefill** is in flight (prefill_count >= max_local, generating_count == 0) passes the provider.py check without queueing, reaches the router, is denied by the prefill gate, and returns HTTP 503 `local_lease_active` → immediate remote fallback.

## Evidence (24h window 2026-09-15 13:49 → 2026-09-16 13:49)

- `local_dispatch_denied` events: 449 (active=1: 373, active=2: 65, active=3: 11)
- `Fallback triggered reason=local_lease_active`: **425** (all fast mode; cheap mode = 0 because cheap has 3 slots and its queue absorbs contention)
- `contention_queue_dispatch`: 1,757 events, median wait **0.00s**, p99 11.4s, max 33.7s, total wait only 498s
- `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`: **6** events (all at the 45s fast cap)

The near-match between deny count (449) and lease-active fallbacks (425), combined with zero `fallback_after_queue` in fast mode beyond the 6 cap-hit cases, indicates most denials never entered the queue — consistent with the prefill gate firing while the generating count was 0.

## Why it matters

Each `local_lease_active` fallback is a request served remotely while the local slot was NOT generating — i.e. capacity the local model could have used. Converting them to local work raises local busy time and cuts remote spend. (Note: prefill is GPU work, so this is not "idle GPU" — but it is serializable work the queue currently discards.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The contention queue wake predicate accounts for the prefill-in-flight count, not only the generating count (either by including `_prefill_count` in `slot_free_check`, or by having the router route prefill-gate denials into the queue).
- [ ] A request denied solely by the prefill gate waits (bounded by `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`) and is dispatched local when the prefill completes, instead of returning `local_lease_active`.
- [ ] Queue wait is still subtracted from the adaptive timeout budget (existing Q2=a contract).
- [ ] Long-prefill guard preserved: the queue must not admit more concurrent prefills than `session_slot_pool_size` (i.e. it must not defeat the prefill-aware guard).
- [ ] Metrics/logging distinguish generating-saturation waits from prefill-saturation waits.
- [ ] Tests cover: prefill-saturated request queues and dispatches; prefill-saturated request exceeding the cap falls back as `fallback_after_queue`.
- [ ] Full test suite green.

## Open question to resolve first

Quantify how many of the 425 fallbacks would have succeeded within the wait cap (i.e. prefill completing within 45s). Large prefills (>45s) will still fall back, so the benefit is bounded by the prefill-duration distribution. Measure before/after on a 24h window.

## Related

- LP-0MTH7JX82000YS5N (generating-only pool + prefill-aware guard — completed; this closes the gap it left)
- LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D (contention queue — policy/caps)
- LP-0MU1S617L002Q9PR (parent: large-context sessions stall/time out)
data.title: Contention queue ignores prefill-saturated dispatches (fast-mode local_lease_active fallbacks bypass the queue)

# Time-window-specific 503 only when every provider was window-skipped

**Parent:** LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO

## Problem

`_build_time_window_exhausted_response` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:2579`) returns the
"no provider is available during the current scheduled time window" 503 when:

- `not any_provider_tried`, AND
- `not unavailable` (no cooldown entries), AND
- **any** recorded attempt has `status == "outside_time_window"`.

It does not verify that the window is the *only* reason. It ignores usage-limit quarantine
(`usage_limit_reset_pending`, which never populates `unavailable`) and local/compaction skips.
During the overnight gaps this produced a message blaming the time window even though the
dominant blockers were usage-limit quarantine and a failed compaction summarizer.

## Change

Fire the window-specific response only when the window is the sole cause — i.e. every
non-tried, non-cooldown candidate was skipped for `outside_time_window`, and no candidate was
skipped for usage-limit quarantine or another reason. Otherwise fall through to
`_build_exhausted_response` (generic "All providers exhausted" with diagnostics).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mixed `outside_time_window` + `usage_limit_reset_pending` skips produce the generic
      `{"error": "All providers exhausted", ...}` response, not the window-specific message.
- [ ] When all providers are outside their window (and nothing else blocks), the window-specific
      message is unchanged.
- [ ] The `diagnostics` list still exposes the `outside_time_window` entries in both cases.
- [ ] New/updated tests in `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py` cover: all-window,
      window+quarantine, window+cooldown, window+local-skip.

## References

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:2579` `_build_time_window_exhausted_response`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:1984` `_providers_outside_window`
- Predecessor: LP-0MS4ETBNO0022QAC

# Chain-hold: bound hold duration by the real retry_after

**Parent:** LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO

## Problem

`_run_chain_cycles` holds an exhausted request for
`server.chain_hold_seconds` (300) × `server.chain_hold_max_cycles` (3) = **15 minutes** and then
returns the exhaustion response, independent of when a provider can actually become available.
During the overnight `available_times` gaps nothing can recover for hours, so the hold is pure
added latency before the client sees the failure. Conversely, a short cooldown (e.g. 2 min) is
over-held.

## Change

Bound the hold by the computed `retry_after`:

- If `retry_after` is within the hold budget, hold at most that long (or the configured hold,
  whichever is smaller).
- If `retry_after` exceeds the budget (or a configured maximum), return the exhaustion response
  immediately with an accurate `Retry-After` rather than holding through cycles that cannot
  succeed.
- Preserve current behaviour for the common short-cooldown case (bounded cycles).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Chain-hold never waits longer than the computed `retry_after`.
- [ ] When `retry_after` is large (window/usage-limit reset), the response is returned without
      exhausting all `chain_hold_max_cycles`.
- [ ] Streaming clients still receive periodic `: chain exhausted (...)` feedback during any hold.
- [ ] Tests assert hold duration tracks `retry_after` for small, medium and large values.

## References

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` `_run_chain_cycles` / chain-hold section (LP-0MSH94Z7K007VKC9)
- `proxy/config.yaml`: `chain_hold_seconds: 300`, `chain_hold_max_cycles: 3`
data.title: Chain-hold: bound hold duration by the real retry_after

# Exhaustion 503: emit a stable machine-readable error code for client classification

**Parent:** LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO

## Problem

The time-window exhaustion 503 carries only a prose `error` string:

    {"error": "All providers unavailable: no provider is available during the current scheduled time window", ...}

The herdr/ContextHub recovery classifier recognises generic `all providers exhausted` and
`no provider available`, but not this wording, so it classifies the error as `UNKNOWN`, surfaces
`Unrecognized error: ...`, and does **not** auto-retry
(`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts`, `register-recovery.ts:184`).

## Change

Return a stable machine-readable contract for every exhaustion path:

- Keep `"error": "All providers exhausted"` (already recognised by clients), and
- add a discriminator field, e.g. `"code": "outside_time_window"` or
  `"code": "all_exhausted"` (and/or `"type"`), plus
- retain `retry_after`, `unavailable_providers`, `diagnostics`, and put human-readable detail in
  a separate `detail`/`message` field so the prose can change without breaking clients.

Do not rely on uniqueness of the `error` prose for client behaviour.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both the time-window path and the generic path return `error == "All providers exhausted"`.
- [ ] A stable `code`/`type` field distinguishes `outside_time_window` from generic exhaustion.
- [ ] `retry_after`, `unavailable_providers`, `diagnostics` remain present where available.
- [ ] Tests assert the JSON contract for both paths (and for the 429 slot-exhaustion path).
- [ ] Follow-up: the ContextHub classifier is updated to key off `code` (separate ContextHub
      work item), not the prose.

## References

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:2579` `_build_time_window_exhausted_response`, `:2535` `_build_exhausted_response`
- Client: ContextHub `recovery/error-patterns.ts`, `recovery/register-recovery.ts:184`
- Predecessor (ContextHub): WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK
data.title: Exhaustion 503: emit a stable machine-readable error code for client classification

# Local lease denial falls through to the remote chain instead of queueing → exhaustion with no client-visible error

**Parent:** LP-0MU56Z3XY001I0NO (overnight remote-chain exhaustion)

## Summary

When the local backend refuses a session because its dispatch lease is held by another session
(`local_dispatch_denied` → `503 server_busy / local_lease_active`), the proxy abandons the local
provider and walks the remote fallback chain. If every remote provider is outside its
`available_times` window (e.g. the 06:00–10:00 UTC gap), the chain is instantly exhausted and the
request is held for `chain_hold_seconds` (300) × `chain_hold_max_cycles` (3) — up to 15 minutes —
with no terminal error delivered to the client. The configured contention-queue policy
(`contention_queue_policy: queue`, `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 120`) is bypassed: the
request is never queued for the local slot that the lease gate is protecting.

## Observed failure (2026-09-17)

Session `herdr-1789635822-3674189-29881` (Pi `/skill:implement`, model `code`) failed while
another session held the local lease. `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` (local time = UTC+1):

```
10:03:44,100 INFO  contention_queue_dispatch provider=local-qwen3 session=herdr-1789635822-3674189-29881 queued_duration=0.00s policy=queue depth=0
10:03:44,110 INFO  routing_check provider=local-qwen3 model=Qwen3 estimated_tokens=11732 cold_threshold=38000 warm_threshold=100000 new_tokens=11732 cached_ratio=0.00 messages=2 session=herdr-1789635822-3674189-29881
10:03:44,119 INFO  [local] POST .../v1/chat/completions body={"model": "code", ...} session=herdr-1789635822-3674189-29881 slot=none
10:03:44,122 INFO  local_dispatch_denied session=herdr-1789635822-3674189-29881 owner=herdr-1789635799-3674044-29198 active=1
10:03:44,122 INFO  Skipping provider=opencode-go-3: outside its available_times window (UTC)
10:03:44,122 INFO  Skipping provider=opencode-go-2: outside its available_times window (UTC)
10:03:44,122 INFO  Skipping provider=opencode-go:   outside its available_times window (UTC)
10:03:44,122 INFO  Skipping provider=deepseek-flash: outside its available_times window (UTC)
10:03:44,122 WARNING All providers exhausted for model=v1/chat/completions; unavailable={}
10:03:44,123 WARNING Chain exhausted ...; holding 300s before restarting cycle (cycle=0, max_cycles=3)
10:03:44,124 WARNING Chain exhausted ...; holding 300s before restarting cycle (cycle=1, max_cycles=3)
```

Corroborating facts:

- The owner session `herdr-1789635799-3674044-29198` (Pi `/intake`) held and continuously renewed
  the lease (`lease_renewed ... timeout=30s`, remaining ≈ 162 s at 10:03:44).
- The proxy was in **fast** mode with `session_slot_pool_size: 1` (`Hard-routing caps: ...
  (mode=fast)`, `slots=1`), so the single local slot was genuinely occupied; in cheap mode (3
  slots) this request would have been admitted.
- The proxy time was 10:03 local = **09:03 UTC**, inside the 06:00–10:00 UTC gap for every remote
  provider (`available_times: ["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`).
- Session recording dir
  `/home/rgardler/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/herdr-1789635822-3674189-29881/` contains only the
  two `*-request.json` files and **no `*-response.json`** — the client received no completion and
  no error before the session ended.
- A second session (`herdr-1789635833-3674406-17592`) hit the identical path 11 s later.

## Root cause / code path

1. `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:1272`) denies the request when the
   generating pool is full (`_generating_count >= max_local`), which is returned by the router as
   a synthetic `503` with `reason: "local_lease_active"` (`router.py:1072-1101`).
2. That response is classified as a retryable **provider** failure and starts the fallback chain
   (`provider.py:3055 _is_local_lease_active_response`, `provider.py:4982`, `provider.py:5391`).
3. The remote tier is entirely out of window, so `_run_chain_cycles` exhausts immediately and
   enters the 300 s hold rather than returning a terminal error quickly.
4. The queue policy never gets a chance to hold the request for a local slot: the
   `contention_queue_dispatch` line shows `queued_duration=0.00s depth=0`, i.e. the request did
   not actually wait, even though `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 120` would have covered the
   lease's remaining lifetime.

## Desired behaviour

- A local lease denial is a **capacity** condition, not a provider failure. While the request's
  own model prefers local and the local queue policy is `queue`, wait up to
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` for the local slot (bounded by the model's adaptive
  timeout) before considering remote fallback.
- If fallback really is required and the chain cannot succeed (all remotes out of window), return
  the exhaustion response promptly with an accurate `Retry-After` instead of holding through
  cycles that cannot succeed (relates to LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08).
- Whatever the outcome, the client must receive a terminal machine-readable error rather than a
  silent multi-minute hold (relates to LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A local-lease denial for a session whose model prefers local and whose mode policy is `queue`
      waits for the configured contention-queue budget (up to
      `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, subject to the adaptive timeout) before attempting
      remote fallback; the queue path logs a non-zero `queued_duration` when it waits.
- [ ] If the local slot frees within the budget, the request is served locally and no remote
      provider is tried.
- [ ] If the budget expires and the remote chain is exhausted (all providers window-skipped /
      unavailable), the client receives a terminal error response (with a machine-readable code and
      `Retry-After`) — not a 300 s × N silent hold.
- [ ] The exhaustion response distinguishes the local-capacity cause (`local_lease_active`) from
      the window cause, so the operator can tell a full slot pool from an out-of-hours gap.
- [ ] Tests in `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py` / contention-queue suites cover:
      lease-denied + queue admits after wait; lease-denied + queue budget expires + all remotes out
      of window → prompt terminal error; lease-denied + remote available → normal fallback.

## References

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:1272` `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py:1042-1101` local dispatch gate / `local_dispatch_denied`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:3055` `_is_local_lease_active_response`,
  `:4342` `_log_chain_hold_start`, `:4380+` `_build_streaming_hold_response`
- `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — `contention_queue_policy: queue`,
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 120`, `available_times` on all remote providers
- Siblings: LP-0MU56ZFII004L7OO (window-specific 503 only when the window is the sole cause),
  LP-0MU56ZKQD005SX08 (bound hold by real `retry_after`),
  LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G (stable error code), LP-0MU5AIAAY003KVM0 (chain-hold does not re-run
  session handling/compaction)
- Failure observed in Pi session `herdr-1789636186-1826695-11871` (investigation of
  `herdr-1789635822-3674189-29881`)

Increase summarizer_max_tokens to 1024 and add client compaction-sync validation

# render_report.py reads auditResult but wl show exposes audit under 'audit' (report always shows 'Audit: not run')

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report renderer never shows the real audit verdict: `render_metadata()` reads `work_item.get("auditResult")`, but `wl show <id> --json` places the structured verdict at the **top level** of the payload (`auditResult.readyToClose`, a boolean), mirroring it into `workItem.audit` (an object with `time`/`author`/`text`/`status` for backwards compatibility) — it is never present as a boolean inside `workItem`. Because `render_from_wl()` passes only `data["workItem"]` to the renderer, the field is always missing and every report renders `- **Audit:** ❔ not run`, even when the work item carries a passing canonical audit.

**Confirmed empirically** on LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB: the top-level `auditResult` is `{..., "readyToClose": true, ...}` and `workItem.audit.status` is `"Complete"`, yet `render_report.py LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB` prints `- **Audit:** ❔ not run`.

## Users

- **Skill agents** (intake, plan, implement, audit, ship) that render the report as their final step and paste it verbatim.
- **Producers/operators** who read reports to decide whether an audit has passed and whether to advance or release a work item.
- **Automation authors** whose scripts and tests consume the rendered report or the documented `auditResult` payload shape.

Example user stories:

- As an **audit/implement agent**, I want the report's Audit line to reflect the persisted verdict, so my final report is not self-contradictory.
- As a **producer**, I want `✅ passed` shown when `auditResult.readyToClose` is true, so I do not waste effort re-running or second-guessing an audit that already passed.
- As an **automation author**, I want the renderer to read the payload shape documented in `skill/report/SKILL.md`, so I can test the report against real `wl show --json` output.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Structured verdict is respected.** Given a `wl show <id> --json` payload whose top-level `auditResult` is `{"readyToClose": true}` (or `false`), the rendered Meta-Data line is `- **Audit:** ✅ passed` (or `❌ failed`). Verified by unit tests over realistic payloads.
2. **Correct wiring on both entry points.** `render_from_wl()` threads the envelope's top-level `auditResult` into the metadata, and the `--json` stdin path handles the full `{workItem, auditResult}` envelope without dropping it. Verified by unit tests that feed a canned envelope (no live `wl`).
3. **Absent / legacy fallbacks.** A null or missing `auditResult` renders `❔ not run`; a legacy boolean `workItem.auditResult` and a legacy `workItem.audit` object (`status: "Complete"`, or text whose first line starts with `Ready to close: Yes`/`No`) still resolve to the correct verdict. Verified by unit tests covering each fallback.
4. **Regression coverage.** A regression test captures the observed failure shape (top-level `auditResult.readyToClose: true`, `workItem.auditResult` absent) and asserts `passed`; re-rendering a real audited item (LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB) shows `✅ passed` instead of `not run`.
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/report/SKILL.md` (the Meta-Data source table and Audit row), and any relevant docs-site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The fix lives in the canonical SorraAgents source `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`; `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/report/` is a symlink to `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/report/` — do not edit through the symlink ad hoc.
- Preserve the public library API: `render_metadata()` / `render_report_from_workitem()` must keep working for callers that pass only a `workItem` dict. New parameters must be optional.
- `auditResult.readyToClose` (top-level, structured) is the authoritative source; `workItem.audit` is a backwards-compatibility mirror only. Do not make `workItem.audit` the primary source.
- Do not depend on live `wl` in unit tests — inject fixtures / patch the subprocess, matching the existing test style.
- Reuse the existing `AUDIT_ICONS` mapping (`yes`/`no`/`unknown`); do not invent new icons.
- Keep the canonical report template contract unchanged: the Meta-Data field name and `- **Audit:**` line stay as-is (only the derived value changes).
- No behavioural drift for already-correct fields (Type/Priority/Status/Stage/Risk/Effort/Children).

## Existing state

- `render_metadata()` (line ~235) reads `work_item.get("auditResult")` and expects a boolean (`True` → passed, `False` → failed). The real payload never has that key inside `workItem`, so it always yields `unknown` → `not run`.
- `render_from_wl()` fetches `wl show <id> --json --children`, then uses only `data.get("workItem", {})` and `data.get("children", [])`; the envelope-level `data["auditResult"]` is discarded.
- The `--json` stdin branch does `work_item = data.get("workItem", data)`, likewise discarding an envelope-level `auditResult`.
- `wl show --json` (ContextHub `dist/commands/show.js` lines ~79–92) sets `result.auditResult = db.getAuditResult(item.id)` and, when present, mirrors it into `result.workItem.audit = {time, author, text, status}`. So the audit is a sibling of `workItem`, not a field on it.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` already documents the correct source: `Audit | auditResult (null → not run; readyToClose true/false)`. The code simply does not implement the documented contract.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` fabricates `"auditResult": true` *inside* the work-item fixture, a shape that never occurs in practice, so no test detected the defect.
- The failed-audit case is symmetric: `auditResult.readyToClose: false` also renders `not run` today, masking `❌ failed`.

## Desired change

Thread the structured verdict from the `wl show` envelope into metadata derivation and normalise the verdict from all known payload shapes.

1. `render_metadata(work_item, children=None, audit_result=None)` — accept an optional structured `audit_result`. Derive `yes`/`no`/`unknown` with precedence:
   1. `audit_result["readyToClose"]` when `audit_result` is a mapping and the key is present (authoritative);
   2. legacy boolean `work_item.get("auditResult")` (keeps callers using simple dicts working);
   3. legacy `work_item.get("audit")` mapping → `status == "Complete"` and/or first line of `text` starting `Ready to close: Yes` / `No`;
   4. otherwise `unknown` → `❔ not run`.
2. `render_report_from_workitem(..., audit_result=None)` — pass `audit_result` through to `render_metadata`.
3. `render_from_wl()` — pass `data.get("auditResult")` into `render_report_from_workitem`.
4. `main()` `--json` stdin path — when the piped payload is the full envelope, pass `data.get("auditResult")` alongside `data["workItem"]`.
5. Tests — replace the unrealistic fixture shape with realistic envelope(s); add cases for `readyToClose` true/false, absent/null, legacy boolean, legacy `audit` object, and the observed regression payload.
6. Docs/comments — update `skill/report/SKILL.md` and the code docstring/comments to state the exact source and fallback precedence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — `render_metadata()` (audit derivation), `render_report_from_workitem()`, `render_from_wl()`, `main()` `--json` branch. Adds optional `audit_result` plumbing and a small verdict-normalisation helper.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — realistic `wl show --json` envelope fixtures; new audit-metadata unit tests (structured true/false, absent, legacy boolean, legacy object, regression case).
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — Meta-Data source-of-truth table (Audit row) and any notes describing the verdict source; confirm it matches the implemented precedence.
- `~/projects/ContextHub/dist/commands/show.js` — read-only reference for the payload shape (`auditResult` top-level, `workItem.audit` mirror); no change expected.

## Related work

- **LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB** — Server-side compaction is unreachable for oversized sessions (the `discovered-from:LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB` item; its passing audit was misreported as `not run`).
- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via helper report skill (umbrella; open, `plan_complete`).
- **SA-0MSRFTP2Y008BH6L** — Create report helper skill with renderer and icon mappings (blocked).
- **SA-0MSRFPUTN0089F3U** — Write tests for report renderer (open; the tests this fix extends).
- **SA-0MSRFTYOI000W0IQ** — Update documentation and verify full test suite (blocked).
- **SA-0MSYYCTPV004MVB1** — fix: `render_report.py` doesn't handle 'adjusted'/'partial' AC verdicts (completed; precedent for renderer correctness bugs).
- **WL-0MMNCOJ0V0IFM2SN** — Audit Read Path in Show Outputs (ContextHub, completed; introduced the structured `audit` read path in `wl show --json`).
- **LP-0MUESDZVW006YJ1N** — StatusLifecycle status normalisation (in-flight; also touches the SorraAgents skill tree — watch for worktree overlap, no logical dependency).

### Related work (automated report)

- **LP-0MSUDLNAK003324R** — [MEDIUM] `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:1491` — Unused `noqa` directive (RUF100) (completed) — *low relevance (keyword co-occurrence only)*.
- **LP-0MSUDLNI700567W3** — [MEDIUM] `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:1730` — Unused `noqa` directive (RUF100) (completed) — *low relevance*.
- **LP-0MSUDLNQ10070FTO** — [MEDIUM] `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:1769` — Unused `noqa` directive (RUF100) (completed) — *low relevance*.
- Repo file matches: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (keyword co-occurrence; useful background on `Ready to close:` parsing).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Choosing the wrong source of truth (text parsing vs structured boolean) could reintroduce ambiguity for manual approvals, whose `summary` is free text (e.g. "Approved by manual review") and may not contain a `Ready to close:` line. **Mitigation:** prefer structured `auditResult.readyToClose`; only fall back to text/`status` for legacy payloads, and cover each path with a test.
- **Risk:** Changing the public signature of `render_metadata`/`render_report_from_workitem` could break external callers. **Mitigation:** new parameters are optional and keyword-defaulted; existing positional calls keep working.
- **Risk:** Tests could keep passing while the CLI path remains broken (the current blind spot). **Mitigation:** add a test that exercises `render_from_wl()` end-to-end against a stubbed `wl show` envelope, not just `render_report_from_workitem()`.
- **Risk:** Scope creep into the audit subsystem (persist/verdict logic). **Mitigation:** this item is read-path only — no changes to `skill/audit/**` or to how verdicts are persisted.
- **Assumption:** The `wl show --json` envelope shape (`auditResult` sibling of `workItem`; `workItem.audit` mirror) is stable for the supported `wl` version (0.1.19) and documented in `skill/report/SKILL.md`.
- **Assumption:** `Audit: not run` must remain the rendering for a genuinely unaudited item (`auditResult` null/absent) — the fix must not fabricate a verdict.
- **Scope creep:** Does not address audit freshness/staleness rendering, TUI audit icons, or the `Audit Read Path` read-cost work; those remain separate items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No operator questions were required — the seed description plus repository inspection were sufficient to draft this brief. The following research-derived answers close what would otherwise have been interview questions (all self-answered; evidence is a file path, command, or work-item id).

- **Q: Where does `wl show --json` actually expose the audit verdict?**
  - Answer: Structured verdict at the payload top level (`result.auditResult`, populated from the `audit_results` table and carrying `readyToClose`), with a backwards-compat mirror at `result.workItem.audit`. Evidence: `ContextHub` `dist/commands/show.js` lines ~79–92; `wl show LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB --json`.
- **Q: Is `workItem.auditResult` ever populated?**
  - Answer: No — it is always absent/null for the current `wl` version, which is why the renderer always says `not run`. Evidence: `wl show LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB --json` ⇒ `workItem.auditResult: None`, top-level `auditResult.readyToClose: True`.
- **Q: Which source should the fix prefer?**
  - Answer: The structured top-level `auditResult.readyToClose`, matching `skill/report/SKILL.md`'s documented contract; text parsing of `workItem.audit` is only a legacy fallback. Evidence: `skill/report/SKILL.md` line ~107.
- **Q: Which repository/path is the canonical source to edit?**
  - Answer: `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`; the `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/report/` path in the bug description is a symlink to it. Evidence: `ls -la /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills` ⇒ symlink to `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill`.
- **Q: Do the existing tests cover this path?**
  - Answer: No — they use a fabricated `workItem.auditResult` boolean and never exercise `render_from_wl`'s envelope extraction. Evidence: `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` lines ~35, ~50.
- **Q: Was the defect reproduced before filing?**
  - Answer: Yes: `python3 .../render_report.py LP-0MU5ARWSP001BYYB` printed `- **Audit:** ❔ not run` for an item with a passing persisted audit. Source: this intake session, command output.
